content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need leaves commercially available chemicals, total price <= $9999.

We have some candidate building blocks: para-methyl aniline (p-toluidine) Cc1ccc(N)cc1 price 28.6 or 115 etc. Also bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (ClSO2PhBr) price 25.3 etc. Also the amide fragment: maybe 4-aminobenzaldehyde? Actually the target has a sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings: one is p-tolyl (with methyl) attached to N of sulfonamide. The other phenyl is para-substituted with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide (C= C - C(=O)N-Ph-NH2). Actually the second phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2) is attached to sulfonyl group. That phenyl has a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline). So we can think of disconnection: break sulfonamide bond to get sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and aniline. Also break the amide bond to get aniline and acid (or acid chloride). Also break the double bond maybe via Heck coupling? But we need <=3 steps.

Potential route:

Step 1: Couple p-toluidine (para-methyl aniline) with 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride? Actually sulfonyl chloride reacts with aniline to give sulfonamide. So we need sulfonyl chloride of the second phenyl (with side chain). So we need to prepare 4-(trans-α,β-unsaturated amide) phenyl sulfonyl chloride. That could be made from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride via Suzuki coupling with side chain? Or we could start from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) and do a Heck coupling with trans-β-aryl acrylamide? But that may be more steps.

Alternative: Build the sulfonamide after installing side chain on phenyl ring via sulfonyl chloride then amide formation later.

Maybe easier: Use sulfonyl chloride of simple phenyl (e.g., 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride) to react with p-toluidine to give sulfonamide with bromophenyl. Then do a Suzuki coupling to attach the side chain (aryl-alkenyl amide). But Suzuki attaches aryl to aryl, not alkenyl amide.

Better: Use a Heck reaction to attach the side chain onto the bromophenyl sulfonamide. That would be step 2. Then final step maybe deprotect? Not needed.

Thus route:

Leaf 1: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) price cheap.

Leaf 2: 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(Br)cc1) price 25.3.

Step 1: React p-toluidine with 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride to give sulfonamide intermediate: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(Br)cc2)cc1.

Step 2: Heck coupling of this intermediate with trans-3-phenylacrylamide? Actually we need to attach /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N onto the bromophenyl. The side chain is trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2 (an anilide). This could be introduced via Heck coupling of the bromophenyl sulfonamide with an acrylamide bearing an aniline. The acrylamide: CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2 (trans). That's a commercially available compound? Search.
